subject: Runtime hop-level telemetry and subprocessor commitments — Q&A
messages:
From: Elsie Turner <elsie@skylinehealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask — where do inference requests actually hop, and who touches tokens?

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re running a short technical review for procurement and security to understand runtime behavior before we finalize the PO. Two quick, concrete asks: 

1) For a typical hosted inference request from our US app, can you provide a hop-level trace that shows which internal services and subprocessors see the request (including any egress to 3rd parties)? We need to show an evidence sample to our risk team.

2) How long might any request or derived KV cache remain at each stage (transient buffer, prefixes, logs)? We need deletion guarantees and owner responsibilities per hop.

Appreciate anything you can share (a redacted trace is fine).

Best,
Elsie Turner
Head of Security Operations
Skyline Health

P.S. We may also need a signed statement for our vendor file — happy to route an MSA addendum if you can confirm the path and retention timings.

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Elsie Turner <elsie@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — where do inference requests actually hop, and who touches tokens?

Hi Elsie — thanks for the clear asks. I’m attaching a redacted trace sample and our subprocessor inventory extract for the US region (see attachments). A couple of clarifying points to help us scope the formal evidence packet: 

- When you say "typical hosted inference request," do you mean our Redwood API in the us-west-2 region using the default model route, or a pinned Dedicated instance? The hop list differs slightly.
- Do you need per-request retention timing (e.g., KV cache lifetime per inference) or just guaranteed maximum times for any transient store and logs?

Quick summary in-line: 
- Hop-level: SDK/client -> Redwood public API edge -> routing proxy -> serving runtime (GPU pool) -> KV cache (in-memory + regional cache) -> optional 3rd-party telemetry aggregator -> return path.
- Subprocessors that may receive telemetry or aggregated logs are listed in the attachment; none of them have access to raw prompt tokens except the serving runtime while processing a request.
- Default transient retention: in-memory buffers are ephemeral (ms–s), KV cache entries default to 1 hour unless you request a shorter TTL; request logs used for troubleshooting are truncated and retained per your configured retention (default 30 days for hosted trial).

Looping in Karthik and Rafael for specifics on deletion proof and a sketch of a signed statement we can provide. If this looks right, we’ll produce a formal evidence packet and an ops-run trace showing a single sample request with timestamps.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elsie Turner <elsie@skylinehealth.com>, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-04T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — where do inference requests actually hop, and who touches tokens?

Hi Elsie — quick technical follow-up from infra: 

On Wed, Nov 3, 2026 at 11:03 AM, camila_reyes@redwood.com wrote:
> - Hop-level: SDK/client -> Redwood public API edge -> routing proxy -> serving runtime (GPU pool) -> KV cache (in-memory + regional cache) -> optional 3rd-party telemetry aggregator -> return path.

A few details to make that concrete for your vendor file: 
- API edge runs in the requested region (we have regional edges in us-west-2 and us-east-1) and does TLS termination; no request bodies are persisted there beyond short-lived buffers.
- Routing proxy may forward requests to a Dedicated pool in the same region or, on capacity fallback, to a compatible model variant in a nearby region. We record routing decisions in ephemeral traces (max 7 days unless flagged for an incident).
- Serving runtime is the only component that materializes token plaintext for model execution; it runs on customer-isolated workloads for Dedicated and in multi-tenant pools for Hosted. For Hosted, we redact customer identifiers in any telemetry sent to aggregators.
- KV cache: in-memory cache lives on the same host as the runtime and is cleared on process termination; regional cache shards on Redis-style stores have TTLs (default 3600s) and deletion is handled via TTL eviction and explicit purge APIs.

For your deletion proof: we can provide a sample purge log (hashed request id references) plus a deleted-objects manifest for the sample trace. Rafael — can you attach the deletion_workflow_diagram_v2.pdf and a short statement we can sign that maps owner responsibilities per hop?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Elsie Turner <elsie@skylinehealth.com>, camila_reyes@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-05T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — where do inference requests actually hop, and who touches tokens?

Hi Elsie — attaching the requested artifacts and a short signable statement. Highlights: 

- We do not send raw prompt or response payloads to external subprocessors as part of normal serving. Telemetry (metrics and sampled, redacted traces) sent to partners is pre-aggregated and excludes user PII and token plaintext.
- Cross-border: Hosted default routing keeps requests in the country/region when you select a regional endpoint; explicit fallbacks to neighboring regions only occur under constrained capacity and are recorded. For customers with residency requirements we recommend Dedicated or a Private deployment.
- Deletion: for the sample trace I’m attaching a purge manifest (hashed ids) showing the TTL eviction and explicit purge call; we can include a notarized log extract under NDA if required.

Attachments: redwood_runtime_hop_trace_sample.txt (redacted), regional_subprocessor_inventory.csv, deletion_workflow_diagram_v2.pdf.

Next steps: Camila — if Skyline wants a one-page signed attestation mapping which Redwood component is responsible for deletion at each hop, we can produce that and route it through legal.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Product Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----
Attachment stubs:
- redwood_runtime_hop_trace_sample.txt (redacted hop-by-hop timestamps, hashed request ids)
- regional_subprocessor_inventory.csv (company, service, region, access type)
- deletion_workflow_diagram_v2.pdf (diagram + owner map)
